text: Affect Destiny Network Strategy April 2024 Affect Destiny Is a network of African churches, ministries, organizations and leaders who are collaborating to raise a missional generation of young people that have been reached with the Word of God, discipled In a local church and commissioned to impact the world. AFFECT DESTINY NETWORK The Affect Destiny Network is an initiative of OneHope, an international ministry with a heart for young people worldwide. For 37 years, we have stood alongside local churches and global partners to catalyze a movement that affects the destinies of children and youth through God’s Word. OUR VISION By 2050, one million churches will lead Next-generation focused churches and empower ten million missional leaders for transformational Impact. 1M One Million Churches 10M Ten Million Missional Leaders The first objective is to partner with and grow alongside one million churches who are focused on the next-generation. By gaining the buy-in of the pastoral leader, we are then able to mobilize the entire church congregation toward the mission of Affect Destiny. The second objective is to mobilize the African Church congregation. To Impact a child’s life and affect the destiny of Africa, we have a vision of raising 10 million missional leaders from the pulpit, to the pews and across every sphere of Influence In society. LEAD HOW DO WE BUILD NEXT-GENERATION CHURCHES? THROUGH 4 PILLARS EMPOWER MISSIONAL TRANSFORMATIONAL BUILDING ON THE RIGHT PILLARS LEADERSHIP Leadership is the guiding principle that every local church will remain committed to investing the right structures and resources that prioritize children and youth ministry and laying the foundation for a thriving next generation. LEADERSHIP Measuring CHURCH INDICATORS: Active children and youth ministry Allocate a percent of budget towards children and youth ministry Appoint a leader or pastor for the children and youth ministry Conduct children and youth-focused church planting MISSIONALITY BUILDING ON THE RIGHT PILLARS Missionality is the guiding principle that encourages the whole Church to embrace the Great Commission to spread the transformative gospel to every corner of the world, prioritizing our children and youth. MISSIONALITY Measuring LEADER INDICATORS: Leader is participating in at least one missional action: Pray, Give & Go Leader is trained in Faith and work integration Leader is actively multiplying disciples within their local community Leader is participating in Kingdom collaboration within their local community EMPOWERMENT BUILDING ON THE RIGHT PILLARS Empowerment is the guiding principle that maximizes mentorship and service opportunities to prepare and equip the leaders of tomorrow, securing our spiritual legacy and future success. EMPOWERMENT Measuring CHURCH INDICATORS: Participate in training for development of skills and capacity for mindset shift In the church Provide opportunity and responsibility to the next generation of leaders In the church Offer Cross-Generational mentorship or discipleship In the church TRANSFORMATION BUILDING ON THE RIGHT PILLARS Transformation is the guiding principle that the African Church can be a divine catalyst for change, leaving an indelible mark on the world by spearheading spiritual and social transformation in the continent and beyond. In order to catalyze a movement In the global Church, we will need a sustainable structure which can support, develop and continue the work of Affecting Destiny for generations to come. 2023 2021 Africa first piloted the concept of durable network by launching a children and youth workers community In Kenya, East Africa. Through this pilot we learned the Importance of the right value propositions, user journeys and advocacy resources which can support our growing relationships. 2022 In 2022, every national leader from the 5 regions gathered In Senegal for an All Africa conference. Here the Initiative of durable networks were more contextually Introduced, using the Insights learned from East Africa. From there forward, all regions began building their networks. In 2023, the Africa Durable Network was officially named “Affect Destiny” Network. It became the convergence point of all ministry strategies to mission fulfillment, and the means to our vision of seeing Africa shed Its old posture of a receiving continent to that of a sending continent as a blessing to the world. AFFECT DESTINY’S TIMELINE WHERE IS AFFECT DESTINY? Affect Destiny Network Is active In all 5 regions across Africa: Southern Africa, Central Africa, Coastal West Africa, East Africa and Sahel Africa. Though not yet active in every African country, the vision is to see the network grow into a widespread movement as the Church comes to learn, understand, and adopt the critical mission of raising a missional generation for transformational impact.

During this time, the Lord gave Bob a vivid vision of the world’s children suffering a vicious attack from Satan. This attack was much more than merely physical— Satan used disease, poverty, abuse, starvation and violence to induce spiritual, psychological, and economical torment upon children as well. This vision from the Lord shattered Bob’s heart and literally left him weeping for the next generation. From this point of deep compassion and brokenness, Bob sought the Lord’s plan for his life, and heard the Lord answer, “I want you to take My Word to the youth and children of the world, and you will do it through leaders.” In response, Bob developed the first Book of Hope, and distributed it to almost one million school children in El Salvador in 1987. By God’s grace, OneHope ministry has touched more than one billion young lives with God’s Word through innovative Scripture tools, using mediumsthat include print, film, apps, virtual worlds, and more. The goal of OneHope is to not just supply temporary relief to reoccurring problems, but rather transform destinies eternally through bringing God’s Word to every child. 2 3 What is Vision 2030? Vision 2030 is a global Church movement to mobilize local churches and leaders to engage every child in every generation with Jesus, through His Word. The movement is made up of churches, ministries, and networks, who are unified in their desire to present the truth of the Gospel to children and youth in their sphere of leadership. The Global Church comes alongside of the local church to create a plan to reach every child by the year 2030 with a strategy in place to continually reach each new generation with the Gospel. The movement aims to empower the local church to advocate on behalf of the young people God has entrusted in their care. What do we measure? “What we measure and how we measure determine what will be considered relevant, and determine, thereby, not just what we see, but what we — and others — do." Peter Drucker Measuring Vision 2030 brings focus and clarity to our mission. There are lots of numbers that help us ensure we are on track to meet

measure determine what will be considered relevant, and determine, thereby, not just what we see, but what we — and others — do." Peter Drucker Measuring Vision 2030 brings focus and clarity to our mission. There are lots of numbers that help us ensure we are on track to meet our goals. We know approximately how many children will "pass through" our target window that we will need to Reach. That number is over 4.4 billion, and represents any child born between 1991-2025. We measure our Gap -- the number of children not currently being reached with God's Word. In addition, we measure: The number of countries we are working in How many church partners we have mobilized The number of leaders trained The level of a child's engagement with Jesus through His Word Vision 2030: Children in Africa Total to be reached in Africa 2010-2030: 938,235,055 Total reached 2010-2019: 230,204,085 Total remaining to be reached 2020-2030: 708,031,014 4 CATALYZING A MOVEMENT Catalyzing a Movement (also known internally as CAM) is a phrase that became integral within the ministry as we developed Vision 2030. It was the realization that we alone cannot hope to achieve our God-given mission to reach every child with God's Word, but rather that mission fulfillment will be accomplished through catalyzing a movement of the Global Church to reach children and youth with the Gospel. This is the work to see the Church reach every child in every generation with Jesus through His Word. Catalyzing a Movement via Vision 2030 is how we will reach every child as part of our God-given mission as a ministry, and sustain the work of reaching every child in every subsequent generation thereafter. The Need 1/3 of the globe has not 3,000+ people groups are 82% of Hindus and heard of Jesus unreached with the Gospel Muslims have never met a Christian personally What does it mean to Catalyze a Movement? Before launching new programs, we ask, “Who is already here? Are we needed? What gaps can we help fill? Who can do this work with us?” Since 2010, we have completed 43 country asset maps answering these questions to ensure we invest our time, resources and focus effectively. And five years in, we are on a trajectory to making Vision 2030 a reality: 88 New countries opened 3 of our top 10 100 million children were “gap”countries surpassed reached in 2015; exceeding their reach goals our projection by 5.5 million! We believe God has equipped us, along with partners new, old and not yet forged, for such a time as this (Esther 4:14). 5 ADAPTIVE PLAN This is how mission fulfillment will be achieved. Because there are so many variables in reaching every child in 200+ different countries and territories, we built an adaptive plan with seven directives to guide and measure our work toward mission fulfillment. It’s not by accident, and we didn’t just get lucky; we realize we have been granted God’s favor to continue doing Kingdom work. Part of that is because we have chosen for our ministry to be Spirit- led and exercise an excellent standard of stewardship by implementing outcome- based ministry. We believe outcome-based ministry design is a Gospel-centered, Spirit-led framework through which we can effectively work to glorify God, love our neighbor, and engage the next generation with the life-changing Word of God. This design guide is a set of best practices and practical tools to help equip you for outcome-based ministry. It covers most of the course material from the Outcome- Based Ministry Design course collection in the order in which you would implement the design process. Our prayer is that this guide will help you pursue fruitful ministry to the glory of God! In ministry, there cannot be faithfulness without the intelligent and intentional pursuit of fruitfulness. CRM – Workbooks Concepts, record types and Data fields Concepts CRM is the acronym used for Customer Relationship Management and refers to the set of practices, business strategies, and technologies focused on customer relationships. A CRM software is a centralized platform to manage all the Organization's relationships and interactions with partners and potential partners, the objective is to improve the customer experience. Workbooks is the CRM platform used in Onehope. Concepts Relational Database: A relational database is a collection of information that organizes data in predefined relationships where data is stored in one or more tables (or "relations") of columns and rows, making it easy to see and understand how different data structures relate to each other. Concepts Workbooks The system records current and potential partner information (such as contact number, address, phone number, role in Organization, etc.), and identifies their activities and contact points with the organization. This includes visits to the site, participation in conferences, telephone calls, emails, notes and various other interactions. It also identifies relationships with other records (People and Organizations). In addition to being a relational database, it is a management tool that helps us: Follow up with partners Update information Carry out activities such as tasks, emails, calls, and meetings Measure progress How can Workbooks help us Catalyze a movement? E.g. Touchpoints - program downloads Feed Download New Workbooks Lead RECORD TYPES Below you will find a brief description of the record types in the system; some records have been customized to meet specific ministry needs according to the region/team use case. E.g. Cohort campaign. Records Records in Workbooks are displayed as forms, which are a collection of information fields. The main record types are: People Organization Lead Opportunity (e.g. VDS Journey) Campaign (e.g. Cohort) Activity Project (e.g. Partnership) Records People A Person record within Workbooks enables you to record and keep track of all the interactions you (and your colleagues) have with other People. In these records, you can store information such as Job Title, Employer, Telephone etc., and the Workbooks user to whom the person record is assigned. For OneHope, a person is typically someone who has already interacted with our network, has participated in training and events, or is familiar with the work OneHope does. People view Records Organization An Organization record within Workbooks enables you to record and keep track of all the interactions you (and your colleagues) have with other Organizations. Within Workbooks we register religious organizations, such as Churches, and other organizations that are related to the work we do. Most of our non-profit organizations are of a religious and/or educational nature, as well as social and humanitarian aid. All of these Organizations will always be related with a person in the system. LIGHT OF THE WORLD LEADER’S GUIDE AN 8-WEEK JOURNEY INTO THE GOSPEL OF JOHN Thank you for your interest in sharing Light of the World with others! A revolutionary way to experience and understand the Gospel, this 8-Week program invites viewers into the last three years of Jesus’ life, as recorded by the Apostle John. This guide has been developed to help you successfully take your students and/or small group through the Gospel of John in 8 weeks. Whether you are utilizing this program for your church small group, as part of a Religious Education program, or will be using it in another setting, the following format is designed to be flexible and allow you to customize the flow of the study for your context with options to watch an entire week’s video all the way through or select specific areas of Scripture as they are outlined below. Whatever your setting, please feel free to adapt the program in any way to best meet the unique needs of your audience. This program was designed to last for 8 weeks. It consists of eight (8) clips that run for approximately 18 to 24 minutes each and covers anywhere from two to three chapters within the Gospel of John. Open each weekly session with a review of the previous week’s contents and ask if there are any questions regarding last week’s content. As the chapter transitions into a new major theme, the viewer will see the title of that theme and the Scripture reference come up on the lower left portion of the screen. Consider pausing during some of the transitions from one topic to another in order to allow the participants to share their thoughts about what they’ve seen. There are suggested questions included to help facilitate that process. You may even want to share what the first discussion question will be prior to starting the video in order to allow the participants to think about it while watching that segment. If you would like to go back at any point and review a specific section return to the main menu on the DVD to navigate to a weekly clip or specific topical sections. This curriculum was created just for you. It was designed to be used with children ages 6 through 12 and can easily be implemented in your Sunday School or Bible Club. The material will challenge children with God’s Word and touch some of the deepest needs of their hearts, including their most basic need for salvation. It will help them seek, know, and understand the nature and character of the one true God. The Stories of Hope Curriculum was designed for three main purposes: • To provide children with an understanding of God’s Big Story. • To address key issues from a Biblical perspective and provide guidance on how to live by the truths found in God’s Word. • To create an opportunity for parents and children to interact while learning Biblical content. God’s Big Story The Bible is not simply a collection of many short unrelated stories. Rather, it is a book of stories that collectively tell the bigger story of God’s relationship with mankind. God created man for his glory, and even though man rebelled and became separated from God, the Bible tells of God’s plan to bring man back to him through his Son, Jesus Christ. To read more about God’s Big Story, see page 174. The corresponding pictures are in the back of this book and can also be found at the back of the children’s book. While the New Testament Scriptures clearly show how God used Jesus Christ to redeem mankind, the Old Testament clearly points to it and shows that this was God’s plan from the beginning. Within Stories of Hope, one in every five Old Testament stories has been chosen to emphasise God’s fulfilment of his plan for redemption through Jesus. Stories of Hope was written to provide children with an explanation of God’s overall plan as seen throughout the entire Bible, using stories from both the Old Testament and the New Testament. Understanding how to use this curriculum is important to successfully implement this programme. This outline will help new facilitators get ready to teach. Be sure you read and understand all of the materials fully and be sure to train facilitators and volunteers so they feel equipped to teach teenagers using Lead Today! When training facilitators, • Distribute the Leader’s Guide. • Invite trainees to spend 3-5 minutes to look through it. • Ask a few trainees to share what topics caught their attention in the Leader’s Guide. • Go through the Introduction to the Lead Today Programme. HOW TO USE THE LEADER’S GUIDE FLOW OF EACH LESSON After the Introductory lesson (Unit 1: Influence), each lesson has the same structure. The sections of each lesson are: PREPARATION REMINDERS: To prepare to teach, review the Scripture and lesson and prepare materials and teaching space. LEADERSHIP QUALITY: Introduces the week’s leadership topic and includes: Key Questions Important questions students should be able to answer when the lesson is completed. • Start out by reviewing the previous week’s key questions • Share any Lifework (homework) students completed during the previous week • Present the new key questions students will encounter during this session Opening Begin each session with opening comments. Read through and become familiar with this in advance so that you are able to present this opening in your own words. This section may contain questions or activities that prompt students to individually or as a group begin thinking about the week’s leadership quality. SCRIPTURE ENGAGEMENT: This section invites students to read the Bible and connect it back to the leadership topic they are currently learning about. GOING DEEPER: This section explains the Scripture story on a deeper level, helping the students understand what they read and how it connects back to the leadership topic of the week. LIFEWORK: This is an opportunity for the facilitator to share a proverb of leadership wisdom and give a summary of what was learned during this lesson. Facilitators should incorporate the Key Questions throughout the lesson and review them one final time at the end of the lesson. Each lesson should conclude in prayer and students should be encouraged to pray about the topic they learned throughout the week. Students should be instructed to read and, if time allows, begin their Lifework assignments. Students should practise and complete their Lifework throughout the week and return the following week prepared to share what they did or what they learned with the rest of the group. text: Training Manual About this Manual Mentoring is an important key in the discipleship of youth. This mentorship training has been developed for use with teens who have completed the Lead Today program. During this 4-hour training, you will equip participants with a foundational understanding of biblical mentorship and strategies for how to successfully build mentoring relationships with young people. About Lead Today: The Lead Today program starts students on a learning journey about leadership. OneHope partnered with John C. Maxwell’s organization, EQUIP, to produce Lead Today, which is working to bring Biblically based leadership training to teens across the globe. Students learn 14 key leadership qualities, study Scriptural examples of these traits in action, and have the opportunity to put them into practice in their own lives. Planning your Training: We have included a recommended schedule for a training event on page 3. You will need a minimum of 4 hours to cover the training content in this manual, plus any needed breaks. If you have additional time, you can lengthen the training by extending Group Discussions, Activities, and the Question and Answer sections. Preparing to Present: Review the suggested script well in advance, and take the time you need to learn it well. Read it out loud and rehearse each section with and without your notes. Plan to speak directly to your audience, not read from the manual. You could even practice by teaching the content to a friend. Before the day of the training, make sure you have gathered all the materials you will need (see page 3) and have planned how you will conduct the activities and group participation sections. If you are using the Teacher’s Workbook, print enough copies for each participant to have one. It is a good idea to have a few extra workbooks just in case you need them. Pair this manual with the accompanying PowerPoint for a complete presentation resource. Note that the PowerPoint is a suggested resource, but you are not required to use it. If you do not have access to a computer in order to display the presentation, you can facilitate the training using just this manual and the Teacher’s Workbook for participants. 2 Training Schedule Below is the suggested agenda for your training. Following this schedule, you will need 4 hours to cover all the training content, plus additional time for breaks as needed. Schedule breaks as makes sense throughout the day. If you have more time available, you can extend Group Discussions, Activities, and the Question and Answer sections. ﻿Unstoppable! Teacher’s Guide Welcome to Unstoppable! Thank you for joining us in this campaign to address the lies that have held so many young women captive and to replace them with the truths found in God’s Word. These lessons are intended for young women between the ages of 10 and 14, but the truths presented are applicable to women of every age. This Teacher’s Guide is designed to be used in association with the Unstoppable! Student Book of Hope. While the lessons in the Book of Hope can be read independently by the students, the lessons inside this Teacher’s Guide have been created to help young adults dig even deeper into God’s Word and the topics discussed. The desired outcomes of this program are that: • Adolescent girls will grow in their trust in God’s Word and gain confidence to speak His promises over their lives. • Adolescent girls will gain renewed hope for the future as they come to understand their identity and value as daughters of God, the love Jesus has for them, and their place in His family. As you teach this program, we pray with joy because of your precious partnership in spreading the Good News. God has begun a good work within you and within your class, and we are certain that He alone is able to carry and complete that good work. Remember that God is faithful to guide and equip you as you commit yourself to opening young women’s hearts and minds to His truth! May He bless and strengthen you for the work He has laid before you! CATALYZING A MOVEMENT By 2050, Affect Destiny Network’s Vision Is to catalyze one million churches who will lead next-generation- focused churches and empower ten million missional leaders for transformational Impact. As a community, we advocate for the spiritual formation and missional unleashing of the next generation. In collaboration with one another, we equip the church with qualified leaders, relevant models, quality resources, a vision for empowerment and growing engagement for strong children and youth ministry. Together, we rise up to God’s calling upon Africa in this time to go from a receiving continent to a giving and sending continent. Our missional generation will take the Gospel again from Africa to the rest of the world. The Affect Destiny Network is an initiative of OneHope, an international ministry with a heart for young people worldwide. For 37 years, we have stood

AFFECT DESTINY NETWORK ABOUT US - 3 NEXT-GENERATION CHURCHES BUILD WITH THE RIGHT PILLARS! Leadership is the guiding principle that every local LEAD church will remain committed to investing the right structures and resources that prioritize children and youth ministry and laying the foundation for a thriving next generation. Missionality is the guiding principle that encourages the MISSIONAL whole Church to embrace the Great Commission to spread the transformative gospel to every corner of the world, prioritizing our children and youth. Empowerment is the guiding principle that maximizes EMPOWER mentorship and service opportunities to prepare and equip the leaders of tomorrow, securing our spiritual legacy and future success. Transformation is the guiding principle that the African TRANSFORMATIONAL Church can be a divine catalyst for change, leaving an indelible mark on the world by spearheading spiritual and social transformation in the continent and beyond. AFFECT DESTINY NETWORK ABOUT US - 4 MISSIONAL LEADERS TRANSFORMATIONAL IMPACT This network desires to participate in the move of the Spirit throughout Africa. Our programs, resources, and research tools develop leaders who are disciples of Jesus and carry His mission to every sphere of influence in their communities and around the world. Africa’s narrative is evolving from receiving to sending. And as stewards of today's youth, we accept our collective responsibility to raise the next generation in Africa into transformative leaders with a missional heartbeat. See one testimony below! M I C K Y ’ S S T O R Y Micky came from a humble background. His father eked out a living as a farmer while his mother sold coffee in the local market. His parents watched helplessly as their son turned to drugs, alcohol, and gambling. Micky fought frequently and failed in school. He knew this wasn’t the future he wanted, but he, too, felt helpless. Training Manual About This Manual This training has been created to empower facilitators and master trainers to teach the Lead Today program. Our goal is for participants to have a thorough understanding of the program and how it functions. This training can be structured as a one-day event for facilitators who will be teaching students, and two days for Master Trainers who will train others. During this time, participants will learn the history of Lead Today, interact with the Leader’s Guide and Student Guide, experience a lesson demonstration, and have an opportunity to put their newly acquired skills into action by teaching others. As you prepare to train, keep in mind that you may have a mixed group of facilitators and master trainers who may or may not be familiar with OneHope. Your participants will likely be thinking about different opportunities to implement Lead Today in their communities. Throughout the training, it is important to communicate strongly and clearly who this program is intended for: literate youth ages 12 -19. Planning your Training: We have included a recommended schedule for your training event on page 3. A facilitator training requires at least 6 hours to cover all the training content. A master trainers training requires a minimum of 12 hours to cover all the content, so we recommend you split that over two days. Note that these estimates do not include tea or meal breaks, which you should schedule as makes sense. If you have time remaining, you can extend group discussions, activities, question and answer sections, and most importantly provide opportunities for participants to teach others. Preparing to Present: • Review the suggested script well in advance and take the time you need to learn it well. Plan to speak directly to your audience, not read from this manual. • As you prepare for the training make sure you are familiar with the details of Lead Today and its history. • Be fully prepared to teach Unit 2, demonstrating what it would be like to teach a room of teenagers. This demonstration will be one of the most important portions of the training. Trainees will use your example as they teach others. If you model a lesson in a dynamic and engaging way, it is our experience that facilitators will replicate up to 70% of what you show them. Your demonstration sets a bar for success, so be sure you are prepared to demonstrate Unit 2 with excellence. • Before the day of the training, make sure you have gathered all the materials you will need (see page 3) and have planned how you will conduct the activities and group participation sections. • Pair this manual with the accompanying PowerPoint for a complete presentation resource. Understanding how to use this curriculum is important to successfully implement this programme. This outline will help new facilitators get ready to teach. Be sure you read and understand all of the materials fully and be sure to train facilitators and volunteers so they feel equipped to teach teenagers using Lead Today! When training facilitators, • Distribute the Leader’s Guide. • Invite trainees to spend 3-5 minutes to look through it. • Ask a few trainees to share what topics caught their attention in the Leader’s Guide. • Go through the Introduction to the Lead Today Programme. HOW TO USE THE LEADER’S GUIDE FLOW OF EACH LESSON After the Introductory lesson (Unit 1: Influence), each lesson has the same structure. The sections of each lesson are: PREPARATION REMINDERS: To prepare to teach, review the Scripture and lesson and prepare materials and teaching space. LEADERSHIP QUALITY: Introduces the week’s leadership topic and includes: Key Questions Important questions students should be able to answer when the lesson is completed. • Start out by reviewing the previous week’s key questions • Share any Lifework (homework) students completed during the previous week • Present the new key questions students will encounter during this session Opening Begin each session with opening comments. Read through and become familiar with this in advance so that you are able to present this opening in your own words. This section may contain questions or activities that prompt students to individually or as a group begin thinking about the week’s leadership quality. SCRIPTURE ENGAGEMENT: This section invites students to read the Bible and connect it back to the leadership topic they are currently learning about. GOING DEEPER: This section explains the Scripture story on a deeper level, helping the students understand what they read and how it connects back to the leadership topic of the week. LIFEWORK: This is an opportunity for the facilitator to share a proverb of leadership wisdom and give a summary of what was learned during this lesson. Facilitators should incorporate the Key Questions throughout the lesson and review them one final time at the end of the lesson. Lead Today: Research Manual the East Africa Region (2018) Research Manual for the Lead T oday Program in East Africa | 1 PROGRAM DESCRIPTION AND OUTCOMES Program Description The Lead Today program is designed to meet a growing global need for biblically-based leadership training. OneHope partnered with John Maxwell’s organization, EQUIP, and produced this program to reverse the current portrayal of poor leadership by offering a desirable portrait of leadership based on biblical principles. Teens can admire, respect, and even aspire to this model of leadership. The Lead Today program connects Maxwell’s leadership teaching with the Bible’s big story, and the program is designed to be used in both schools and churches, targeting teens between the ages of 12 and 19. This Lead Today research will encompass the full 15-unit program. Program Outcomes After completing the Lead Today program, participants will be able to: 1. Practice leadership and develop their skills. Training Manual About this Manual Mentoring is an important key in the discipleship of youth. This mentorship training has been developed for use with teens who have completed the Lead Today program. During this 4-hour training, you will equip participants with a foundational understanding of biblical mentorship and strategies for how to successfully build mentoring relationships with young people. About Lead Today: The Lead Today program starts students on a learning journey about leadership. OneHope partnered with John C. As the gatekeepers of local churches, pastors hold the keys to unlocking their congregants building a strong spiritual Heritage for the body. Parents are the most influential voice over the lives of their children. It is critical to invest in parents so they are best equipped to disciple their children and youth. (Spark) Children & Youth workers are equipped, trained, and connected in a growth community can implement relevant tools, resources and models to their local church. Every community must have a church where children and youth can be raised to expand God’s family and God’s kingdom. Innovators can build missional solutions and relevant programs for the Church which respond to the changing realities of the next generation. ONE NETWORK | SIX EXPRESSIONS LEAD MISSIONAL The Church leadership is establishing structures to invest in children and youth ministry as one of or the main focus of the church TRANSFORMATIONAL The Church is creating opportunities and mentorship in the church to equip, disciple and enable the success of the next-generation of leaders Leaders in the whole church who have a mindset of taking the whole gospel to the children and youth of the whole world Affect Destiny Network is a God-driven agent bringing spiritual & social transformation of Africa to impact the world. BUILT ON 4 PILLARS EMPOWER MISSIONAL Target Audience: Bishops, senior pastors and associate pastors in the local church PASTORS EXPRESSION “Mobilizing pastors to lead next-generation focused churches and empower missional leaders for transformational impact.” PASTORS EXPRESSION OUTCOME SENIOR & ASSOCIATE PASTORS An Opportunity to engage church leadership We understand that churches have a variety of leadership structures that reflect their vision, capacity and priorities. Senior pastors will gain a clear understanding of the vision of Affect Destiny and be invited to explore ways to participate through upcoming events or partnerships. Senior pastors will grasp the urgency of Africa’s missional role and commit to reaching beyond the walls of the Church. Case Studies CASE STUDY 1 “...it is not the case that Paul engages in tent making as a necessity so that he can do his ‘real job’ of preaching. Instead Paul’s varieties of work in the sewing shop, marketplace, synagogue, lecture hall, and prison are all forms of witness. In any of these contexts, Paul participates in God’s restorative project.” “Even if he (Paul) had not had the gift of being a Preacher and Apostle, he still would have been a witness to Christ simply by the way he engaged in making tents, toiling for the sake of the community, and working for the good of others in all situations.” The Theology of Work (TOW) Project What lessons can be drawn from Apostle Paul’s example on integrating faith and work as a pattern for marketplace missions? text: Introduction to Pastor’s Roundtable Roundtable Overview This roundtable discussion content is designed to be used among pastors, each roundtable conversation is meant to last two hours. Africa has historically been postured as a receiving continent in regard to Missions, but in recent decades, Africa is rising as a key centre of Mission and missionality toward the rest of the world. Indeed, to whom much was given, much is being required. In this roundtable, pastors will discuss a rich theology of missionality inside and outside the church based on the Scriptures. The aim is to provide a forum of robust discussion and leave with helpful frameworks that apply the concept of missionality to the local church and inspire collaborative action across the African church. Link to Affect Destiny Introduction video here. Roundtable Outcomes Leaders will gain a robust understanding of missionality as it applies to the African church today. Leaders identify the role they can play both individually and corporately to become and raise missional leaders for transformational impact. How to Lead the Roundtable Conversation This roundtable includes short video showings, so it is advised to download the video and be prepared with a screen or projector. Video clips can also be shared to Pastors via Whatsapp for individual viewing. Facilitators are encouraged to watch the video beforehand and prepare short summaries in case of technical challenges. This manual includes symbols to help you guide the roundtable conversation. The icons and what they mean are listed in the Icon Guide on page 3. Previous Roundtable Review The review aims to create a rhythm from the previous discussion. The flow will aid better understanding and evoke stronger convictions. They will develop an awareness of the need to position themselves for the unique responsibility of Missions; and be better equipped to help their church. text: ESSENTIALS OF YOUTH MINISTRY Training Manual FOUNDATIONS ABOUT THIS MANUAL This manual is a targeted view of youth ministry. It will address several of the main areas in which OneHope feels it is important to prepare teachers who work with young people and will deepen your knowledge of Youth Ministry. After participating in the entire Essentials of Youth Ministry presentation, an attendee should be able to: 1. Identify the physical, intellectual, emotional and spiritual developmental milestones associated with teens and be able to adjust their teaching style to meet this age group’s unique needs effectively. 2. Understand the power of using Scripture in teaching and how to strengthen Scripture engagement in the lives of teens so that it will remain with them throughout adulthood. 3. Recognize and apply the power of a personal testimony to their lesson planning and mentoring. 4. Understand the Biblical model of mentoring and how to initiate and maintain effective mentoring relationships with select teens. 5. Identify practical next steps to apply the information they learned in this training to their ministry. Teachers have a unique and influential role in helping youth discover God’s plan for their lives. The material presented in these modules is designed to provide you with a framework to do just that. This training is designed to be interactive so that attendees have the opportunity to share their successes and challenges in teaching teens. Text and activities are designed to be modified to reflect and meet the unique cultural needs of your audience. There are several sections marked with the plus icon where you will have the chance to customize the material or create your own activity. This will allow you to personalize the material for your audience and your community. It is not required to teach all the modules within Essentials of Youth Ministry. Based on the training needs of your audience and the time available, you may choose to teach all of the material or only select modules. We highly recommend that you include the module Practicing Spiritual Disciplines in every training. Each module has a Knowledge Check form included at the end. If you are only teaching select modules, it is a good idea to have participants complete this as a helpful review of what they have learned. If you are teaching the entire presentation, you can choose to use the Feedback Form instead. This serves as a comprehensive review of the entire training presentation along with a few questions about the effectiveness of your teaching. THREE-DAY A three-day training for those guiding children around the world to follow Jesus like the twelve disciples VOLUME I INSTRUCTOR’S GUIDE Part of the 1for50 family of training resources Revised February 2020 THREE-DAY TWELVE INSTRUCTOR’S GUIDE About this Training What if every child in every community had someone to reach, disciple and empower them to become an influential Kingdom Champion? This is the dream of the 1for50 Movement. And we believe it is possible, because this is God’s dream, not ours. This three-day 1for50 training is designed to equip children’s ministry teachers and leaders. After completion of this training, participants will possess a strong biblical foundation for children’s ministry and have practical teaching skills to effectively reach, disciple and empower children in their church, community outreach program, NGO or other ministry. We want leaders to get the most out of participating in this three-day training. Adults are practical and learn best when they can participate, collaborate and bring their life experience to the training. For that reason, much of the lesson content is discussion and activity based, with guidelines for the trainer to help discussions stay on topic. Lessons have been written so they can be taught individually or together in a module, depending on the amount of time you have. If using the lessons for a three-day training, it is best to teach them in the order they have been written. Please feel free to adapt individual lessons for your unique training style, culture and context. As you make changes, always keep the lesson objectives in mind. Note, however, that for your training to be considered an official 1for50 training, you must include the 1for50 vision and an invitation to either learn more about 1for50 or to join in the movement. (See the Invitation Guide on page 108 for more details.) After your training is completed, please reportify (report and testify) on your event. You can reportify by sending a report to your 1for50 Regional Champion, emailing the 1for50 Global Leadership Team at 1for50@gmail.com or by filling in the online Activity Form. (www.1for50.net/active) 2 THREE-DAY TWELVE INSTRUCTOR’S GUIDE How to Use This Manual As you prepare to teach each lesson, prepare your own heart with prayer. Ask God to open hearts of participants and to help you share from your heart about the topic. Read through each lesson and the Scriptures used in the lesson. Also gather or prepare the materials listed for the lesson. THREE-DAY A three-day training for those guiding children around the world to follow Jesus like the twelve disciples VOLUME I INSTRUCTOR’S GUIDE Part of the 1for50 family of training resources Revised February 2020 THREE-DAY TWELVE INSTRUCTOR’S GUIDE About this Training What if every child in every community had someone to reach, disciple and empower them to become an influential Kingdom Champion? This is the dream of the 1for50 Movement. And we believe it is possible, because this is God’s dream, not ours. This three-day 1for50 training is designed to equip children’s ministry teachers and leaders. After completion of this training, participants will possess a strong biblical foundation for children’s ministry and have practical teaching skills to effectively reach, disciple and empower children in their church, community outreach program, NGO or other ministry. We want leaders to get the most out of participating in this three-day training. Adults are practical and learn best when they can participate, collaborate and bring their life experience to the training. For that reason, much of the lesson content is discussion and activity based, with guidelines for the trainer to help discussions stay on topic. Lessons have been written so they can be taught individually or together in a module, depending on the amount of time you have. If using the lessons for a three-day training, it is best to teach them in the order they have been written. Please feel free to adapt individual lessons for your unique training style, culture and context. As you make changes, always keep the lesson objectives in mind. Note, however, that for your training to be considered an official 1for50 training, you must include the 1for50 vision and an invitation to either learn more about 1for50 or to join in the movement. (See the Invitation Guide on page 108 for more details.) After your training is completed, please reportify (report and testify) on your event. You can reportify by sending a report to your 1for50 Regional Champion, emailing the 1for50 Global Leadership Team at 1for50@gmail.com or by filling in the online Activity Form. Abuse can come in many forms, such as: physical or verbal maltreatment, injury, assault, violation, rape, unjust practices, crimes, or other types of aggression. Bullying Behaviour that is repeated over time, includes deliberately harmful or aggressive behaviour and involves a power imbalance between the victim of the bullying and the perpetrator of the bullying. Injury or discomfort is inflected through physical contact, verbal attacks or psychological manipulation. Bunking A learner takes unauthorised absence from school. Boycotting A learner refuses to cooperate with or participate in a class activity or school event. Child-friendly education An education system that upholds the best interests of the child. Education systems and schools should be designed and run in a way that ensures that all children can learn in a safe, healthy, secure, stimulating and protected environment. Code of conduct A collection of rules and regulations that include what is and is not acceptable or expected behaviour. Corporal Punishment Any punishment in which physical force is used and intended to cause some degree of pain or discomfort, however light. Child A person under the age of 18. Drug trafficking The sale and distribution of illegal drugs. Exploitation To take unfair and, often, unlawful advantage of a person. Educator A person who provides instruction or education and who is registered as such in terms of regulations or legislation. 3 SCHOOL DISCIPLINE GUIDELINES Grievous bodily harm Serious physical injury inflicted on a person by the deliberate action of another. Inclusivity Embracing everyone regardless of their race, gender, age, sexual orientation, where they come from or any other characteristic. Learner A person enrolled in a school who attends classes in order to attain an appropriate level of mastery of a subject under the guidance of an educator. Maltreatment Cruel or violent treatment of a person. Misbehaviour Behaviour that does not meet with rules and what is considered acceptable behaviour. Moderate chastisement Any punishment that causes pain but not injury. Positive Discipline A discipline model used by schools, and in parenting, that focuses on the positive points of behaviour. Vandalism An action involving deliberate destruction of or damage to public or private property. 4 FOREWORD The Ministry of Education and Training in an effort to promote safe, non-violent and protective enabling environment in Eswatini schools, has taken a stand to abolish all forms of corporal punishment in the school setting. The Ministry is replacing it with Positive Discipline (PD). The Ministry has therefore developed these guidelines to hand hold schools towards implementing the ethos of positive discipline. These Guidelines provide a clear guide to schools on alternative, positive methods of disciplining learners. It outlines the principles of positive discipline and how to respond to inappropriate behaviour with regards to the different levels of misbehaviour and consequences. Corporal punishment models violence, aggressiveness, hostility, fear and revenge. This disrupts the process of child development and against the standards of the teaching profession. It also has negative long term effects if not addressed appropriately. PD aims at allowing the child to learn self-discipline and respect for others without fear and enable them to take responsibility for making good decisions and understand why these decisions are in their best interest. The introduction of PD in schools is informed by the fact that the Kingdom of Eswatini, is a signatory to the Conventions on the Rights of the Child (CRC), and therefore has to put in place administrative measures upholding the rights of a child as per Article 19 (1). The guidelines aligns to the National Legislative measures in place, which are the Children’s Protection and Welfare Act 2012 and Sexual Offences and Domestic Violence Act 2018 amongst others. text: 10 keyS to evangelizing members of cultic groups No one can know every false teaching of every cult, but Christians who learn the Bible well can develop their abilities to recognize cultic doctrine. Know what you believe and why.  Know basic Bible teachings. 10 Keys to Evangelizing Members of Cultic Groups Example: Some bankers receive training to easily recognize the characteristics of genuine dollar bills so they can easily recognize counterfeit money.  Know basic Bible teachings. 10 Keys to Evangelizing Members of Cultic Groups “But even if we or an angel from heaven should preach to you a gospel contrary to the one we preached to you, let him be accursed.” Galatians 1:8  Know basic Bible teachings. 10 Keys to Evangelizing Members of Cultic Groups  Don’t assume that every cultist believes all the same things about their group. Even members of the same group may have different levels of knowledge (or opinions). Ask the individual about their personal beliefs; don’t accuse them of believing this or that particular false doctrine. 10 Keys to Evangelizing Members of Cultic Groups  Cultists are often trained to answer objections. For example, Jehovah’s Witness and Mormon missionaries can seem like they know the answer for everything you say. But often what they really know is their own doctrinal system, plus some Bible prooftexts and a rehearsed speech that makes them appear to know more than they actually do. 10 Keys to Evangelizing Members of Cultic Groups  Check the Scriptures. Cultists often quote Bible verses out of context. Carefully verify the meaning of any Bible passages they use by reading the verses before and after— or when appropriate, the entire chapter. 10 Keys to Evangelizing Members of Cultic Groups  Deﬁne important terms. Cults often give new meanings to common Christian words and expressions like “God” and “salvation.” You can minimize confusion and remove this communication block between yourself and the cult member by carefully deﬁning the meaning of key Christian words and ideas. 10 Keys to Evangelizing Members of Cultic Groups  Ask strategic questions. You can’t force good doctrine on a person who is spiritually trapped in a cultic group. But you can kindly ask questions that help them to think critically about what they’ve been taught. 10 Keys to Evangelizing Members of Cultic Groups  Be loving and patient. It’s not just what you say, it’s how you say it! Be courteous and respectful at all times —even if the cultist is not. text: CRAWLING OFF THE ALTAR Student ministry is very demanding, yet the fruit seems not to come immediately. Teachers easily get discouraged, it's not an appealing ministry coupled with less recognition and appreciation. Sometimes discouraging as one don't see progress among the very students he is working with. The session objectives are: 1. What can hold the teacher to keep going, when the going becomes tough? To remain at 'the altar' of faithful service? 2. How do we encourage teachers who have 'crawled off the altar' or been discouraged? Because of distractions that come from pursuing investments, or easier life of convenience. CRAWLING OFF THE THE HIGH CALLING OF GOD JULY 6, 2022 TEXTS: PHILIPPIANS 3:5-21; EPHESIANS 4:1 INTRODUCTION Scripture tells the stories of several persons whom God called, their response to God’s call, and the results of their obedience. But to properly understand and embrace the high calling of God, it is important to first understand the nature of a call. In the context of this study, a call is an invitation, a summons; it is to beckon to something or someone or someplace. Answering a call result in an encounter with the caller and his/her agenda – a meeting point with whoever or whatever that gave the call. Depending on the nature and intent of the caller and the call, the call generates consequences – positive or negative for the person called and others affected by the call. A call offers an opportunity, an assignment, a benefit, etc. depending on its purpose. Our response to a call is measured by the who, why, what, where, when of the call. This will include the following: 1. The Caller: the authority, level, character, status, etc. of the caller and our perception and estimation of them impacts on our response. This is directly applicable to our attitude to and response to God’s call: our revelation of His person will determine what we do with His call. Who’s at risk of addiction?/Increased vulnerability • Genetic predisposition. This theory has little evidence to support it, but is postulated especially since addiction crosses social divides. • There are also cultural and social factors that put people at greater risk. For instance, you’re less likely to become alcohol-dependent growing up in a country where alcohol consumption is unacceptable than where it’s a normal part of everyday life. • Growing up in a family where there’s alcohol or drug abuse increases the risk. • People who suffer childhood trauma, abuse and neglect. Who’s at risk of addiction? • Poverty, a lack of education and unemployment can also increase the risks. If your environment is stressful and you feel unable to change it, you may turn to substances for relief. • Significant life events may contribute. If your inner world is in turmoil, you may turn to substances as medication to feel better. Poor coping mechanism. • People who don’t receive adequate nurture as children or who are more emotionally sensitive may be more susceptible. Reasons why school going children are using drugs • Peer pressure. They are now influenced by their friends. • Pressure from academics. The education system seems to be taking a toll on our children and they can end up using drugs and alcohol as a means of escape. • Parents are not supervising their children. Parents especially in urban areas are busy working. In addition, the lack of community ownership in these urban areas leaves children with a gap to explore the use of drugs and alcohol. Reasons why school going children are using drugs - 2 • Easy accessibility to drugs. Is your real purpose as a teacher just to have students know the dates of the 2nd world war, how to write a sentence or divide and multiply? An effective educator uses their skills, expertise and advantage not only to teach thinking skills and develop minds and helping students to pass, but also to nurture, inspire, encourage and positively influence their students Can a Christian teacher be consistently diligent while maintaining excellence? Objectives What does the Bible say about diligence and excellence How can we model diligence and excellence as Christian teachers to students What is the impact of laziness and mediocrity in the teaching profession Diligence: The quality of working carefully and with a lot of effort Quality - how good or bad something is Working - is about the work itself that you do Carefully - means with great attention Effort - is indicative of physical and mental activity needed to achieve something, persistent exertion of body and mind. constant and earnest effort to accomplish what is undertaken; It is a virtue that describes thoroughness, carefulness, zeal, commitment, tirelessness, studiousness. Can be indicative of a work ethic, that is the belief that work is good in itself. Excellence - the quality of being outstanding or extremely good, truly being the best about something Is about distinction, high quality, mastery, expertness, supremacy, eminence #1. and YM101 Training Events in Uganda | 3 OVERVIEW Background CM1011 and YM1012 are five-module training programs developed by the OneHope training team to help ministry workers and volunteers understand why it is important to minister to children and youth and how to minister effectively. In September 2019, training facilitators in Uganda held a one-day CM101 event in the Kampala district at Born Again Fellowship in Nateete. Additionally, facilitators held a two-day event in Lira at the Pentecostal Assemblies of God (PAG) Lira. The first day of the Lira event focused on CM101 and the second day focused on YM101. Training Atmosphere The training facilitators shared that the churches in the Kampala and Lira areas only recently turned their attention to children’s and youth ministry, and that the concept is not always viewed positively by church administrations. The facilitators also noted the need for more time, especially when filling out surveys, and the need for materials to be translated into a local language. However, the trainers believed all the modules of the training were impactful, especially the Gospel modules. Purpose of the Research The purpose of the research is to evaluate the effectiveness of CM101 and YM101 in East Africa. Therefore, this evaluative research aims at addressing the following research questions: 1. Are CM101 and YM101 being implemented as intended? 2. What modules are trainers typically utilizing during trainings? 3. Are the training outcomes CM101 and YM101 being achieved? 4. How are the training participants applying the training content to their ministries? This report summarizes the results of the September 2019 research, which supports questions one through three. Additional research will be conducted digitally or, if necessary, through the help of the East Africa team to address question four. Methodology The following methodological strategies were implemented in order to address this study’s research questions. • Pre- and Post-Training Survey – CM101 and YM101 participants completed an eight-question pre-survey prior to the start of the training to gather initial content knowledge. At the end of the training, they completed a post-survey which included the same eight content knowledge questions. Comparing responses between the pre-survey and post-survey measures content knowledge growth. • Post-Training Implementation Survey – Completed by the Children’s Ministry and Youth Ministry training facilitators to gather information on the modules included in the training as well as feedback regarding the effectiveness of the implementation. • Post Training Follow-Up Digital Survey or Phone Interview – Will be completed by Children’s Ministry and Youth Ministry track participants to gather

These youth are reached with the Word of God, discipled within local churches, and equipped to make a global impact. The Affect Destiny Member Survey was conducted to gain insights into the network’s members who minister to children and youth in Burundi, Kenya, Rwanda, South Sudan, Tanzania, Ethiopia, and Uganda. The survey focused on ministry activities and programs aligned with the network’s four pillars: Leadership, Missionality, Empowerment, and Transformation The findings will be used to identify gaps and opportunities for ministry, enabling Affect Destiny to better support its members by addressing their needs and guiding strategic decisions. Additionally, partners will leverage the research bethannwilliams@onehope.net as a planning tool to understand the strengths and challenges in children and youth ministry across the region. Methodology Digital and paper survey versions were shared with members of the network across different countries. Paper surveys were then collected and entered into Alchemer. The world’s current generation of teens and young adults is sometimes called Generation Z. Across Uganda, there are more than 8.2 million Generation Z teens ages 13-19 comprising 17% of the population.1 This research reveals the beliefs, habits, influences, and struggles of the teens across Uganda. The research also reveals their views of God, Jesus, the Bible, and the church. Data was collected across rural, semi-urban, and urban parts of Uganda in March 2022. This project was a follow-up from a larger global study that surveyed teens across more than 20 countries, including the African nations of Kenya, Nigeria, and South Africa. Modified versions of this survey have also been conducted in 10 additional African countries. We hope you not only learn something new, but that your mind and heart are moved to action on behalf of this generation who so need the hope of the Gospel in their lives. Every statistic in this study represents individual teens with their own sets of hopes, fears, and daily challenges. Each of those teens has a name, a story, and an eternal destiny.
